swTimeline.title: Ohara
swTimeline.description: Interactive Software Engineering timeline connecting patterns, anti-patterns, and paradigms through primary sources and constellation visualizations.
swTimeline.blurb: Born from a simple question: where does each idea in software actually come from? Ohara maps the genealogy of computing as a directed acyclic graph of primary sources — from Turing (1936) to modern distributed systems — turning scattered papers into guided study trails.
highlights: Topological sort with cycle detection over the citation graph
Verified primary sources only — provenance-labeled, never invented
Accessible & responsive: keyboard-navigable nodes, reduced-motion aware
Decoupled by design: external-configuration pattern, tested with Vitest

kafkaViz.title: Kafka Viz
kafkaViz.description: Real-time visual simulation of an Apache Kafka cluster — topics, partitions, producers and consumers with animated messages.
kafkaViz.blurb: Distributed messaging is hard to grasp from a static diagram. Kafka Viz turns an Apache Kafka cluster into a living picture — watch messages flow through topics and partitions, consumer groups rebalance, and offsets advance in real time.
highlights: Faithful model of partitions, consumer groups and offsets
Smooth, real-time animation of message flow
Consumer lag and message routing visualized live
Built in React + TypeScript, zero backend required

angularDemo.title: Angular Demo
angularDemo.description: Tech Stack Explorer built with Angular 17+ using standalone components, Signals, Reactive Forms and HttpClient demonstrating real-world patterns.
angularDemo.blurb: A focused showcase of where Angular is heading. Built on Angular 17+ with standalone components and the new control flow, it demonstrates modern, testable patterns end to end — no NgModules, no boilerplate.
highlights: Standalone components with the new @for / @if control flow
Reactive state with Signals — fine-grained, predictable updates
Typed Reactive Forms and HttpClient with real-world structure
Maintainable & testable: clear separation of concerns
